question: Can an isolated writable Cirrove FUSE mount create and preserve one run-owned file in the Workspace Shared Drive across a daemon crash and restart?
kind: Pre-registered bounded live functional probe; a temporary gate bypass is confined to a detached worktree and private binary, not the installed daemon or review branch.
authorization: The owner requested all work needed to continue Google testing and authorized a dedicated Shared Drive. Mutations are limited to a new UUID-named folder within Cirrove Test; no existing Workspace content is changed.
source_revision: c9f25c951c44f10f02e7b2d383ec13a72e31a5d1 plus a local-only writable Shared Drive gate bypass
isolation: Separate Cirrove state, new account UUID, disabled installed-daemon access to this state, private FUSE mount and disk-backed TMPDIR/SQLITE_TMPDIR. The existing cirroved service and its three mounts remain untouched.
arms: A: start the private daemon with one writable Shared Drive account, create a UUID-named folder and a small deterministic file through FUSE, fsync, and require uploaded status plus exact remote bytes

B: stop only the private daemon by its recorded PID during a second run-owned save, restart that daemon from the same private state, then require durable upload completion and exact remote bytes without duplication
C: confirm the original file remains addressable and content-identical, and no installed account or mount changed
endpoint: A passes only with exact scoped provider identity, uploaded state and matching SHA-256. B passes only if the journal survives the private daemon crash, the restart completes or safely reconciles the same exact item, and the final SHA-256 matches with no duplicate sibling. On any uncertainty stop, retain all run-owned items and state, and keep normal Shared Drive writes blocked.
prediction: The new exact-reconciliation fallback should handle an uncertain upload receipt, but FUSE writeback or restart may expose a separate Shared Drive assumption.
limits: One account, one drive and two small run-owned files cannot establish multi-user safety, long-session reliability or all filesystem operations.
temporary_filesystem: btrfs under /home; private TMPDIR and SQLITE_TMPDIR were not tmpfs

result.arm_a: The isolated writable FUSE mount created a UUID-named folder inside the existing Cirrove Validation folder and a 68-byte file. The mutation and transfer journals reached Applied and Uploaded. Independent Google API reads matched exact item, parent and Shared Drive identities, size and SHA-256.
result.arm_b: A second run-owned 16,777,263-byte file was fsynced through the mount. Immediately before killing only the private daemon by its recorded PID, the journal showed one Uploaded and one Uploading operation. The restarted private daemon recovered the disconnected FUSE mount, reached ready and the second operation reached Uploaded. An independent Google API read matched exact item, parent, drive, size and SHA-256; a scoped sibling query found exactly one file with that name.
result.arm_c: After restart, both files read through FUSE with their original byte counts and SHA-256 hashes. The private daemon stopped cleanly and its FUSE mount disappeared. The installed daemon and its three ordinary mounts were not restarted.
result.interpretation: This closes the bounded one-account mounted-create and interrupted-upload gate. It does not establish whether the second upload committed before or after SIGKILL, only that the journal completed or reconciled it after restart without a duplicate. The production Shared Drive write gates were not changed for this probe.

remaining: Before a general writable Shared Drive release, test conflict and rename/move/delete through an isolated mount, a second account or permission level, and a longer session. Keep the ordinary account read-only until the proposed production gate change is reviewed and installed separately.
followup_question: Do the mounted Shared Drive rename, move, replacement and observed-empty delete paths preserve exact identities and bytes on run-owned objects?
followup_arms: D: create a new UUID-named folder and binary file through a separate isolated writable mount, wait for exact uploaded identities, then rename the file and verify the exact ID did not change
E: create a nested destination folder, move the file into it, replace its bytes through the mount, and verify the same exact Google item, parent, name and SHA-256
F: delete only that run-owned file through the mount, verify its exact Google item is trashed, then remove the observed-empty run-owned folders and verify their exact IDs are trashed
followup_endpoint: Each mutation must reach the durable Applied or Uploaded state with zero stuck changes and independent exact-ID Google readback. A failed or uncertain operation is retained for review; no pre-existing item is changed. The installed daemon and normal Shared Drive write gate remain untouched.
followup_prediction: The shared mutation path should handle run-owned rename and move, but Shared Drive trash and nested folder parent responses may differ from My Drive.
production_gate_control: The enabled Shared Drive write-grant test failed on the pre-enable source with 'invalid selected Google Drive' and passed after the account validation and provider gates were changed. The live mount probes used a local-only binary with those same two gates opened. Desktop sign-in and selection with a Shared Drive write grant have not yet been exercised live.

followup_result.arm_d: The separate isolated mount created a UUID-named folder and a 32,773-byte binary file, then renamed the file. Independent Google API reads confirmed exact item, parent and Shared Drive IDs, original SHA-256 and unchanged item ID after rename.
followup_result.arm_e: The mount created a nested destination, moved the same file into it with a new name and replaced its content with 65,543 deterministic bytes. The transfer reached Uploaded. Independent exact-ID Google readback confirmed the same item, new parent and name, and replacement SHA-256.
followup_result.arm_f: The mount unlinked only the run-owned file, then removed the two observed-empty run-owned folders. Each mutation reached Applied. Independent Google API reads with exact IDs confirmed all three items were trashed in the selected Shared Drive.
followup_result.private_final_state: Ready, one private mount while running, two Uploaded transfer records, seven Applied mutation records, zero failed uploads and zero stuck changes. The private daemon stopped cleanly and its FUSE mount disappeared; the installed daemon and ordinary mounts were untouched.
followup_result.boundary: One Workspace administrator on one owned drive. Concurrent edits, restricted roles, long sessions and real application save patterns on Shared Drives remain unverified. A preview can expose writes with that stated limit; this record does not prove broad provider reliability.
